dave_customer: hey @support — after we bumped to ts-sdk@0.9.4 our /rerank responses started containing unexpected scores. sometimes '0', sometimes 'NaN', and occasionally scores come back as strings. started after the release yesterday. minimal repro below.

alice_support: sorry to hear that — can you paste the request body + sdk version + a server response?

 dave_customer: sure. ts snippet we use (very small):
 ```ts
 import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference';
 const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
 await c.rerank({
   query: 'find best answer',
   candidates: ['A', 'B', 'C'],
   model: 'rerank-small',
 });
 ```
 we also tried python:
 ```py
 from redwood import RedwoodClient
 rc = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['RW_KEY'])
 rc.rerank(query='find best answer', candidates=['A','B','C'], model='rerank-small')
 ```
 server response (truncated):
 ```json
 {
   "scores": ["0","0","NaN","1"],
   "parsed_candidates": 4
 }
 ```
 note parsed_candidates=4 but we sent 3.

 ben_engineer: hmm looks like an extra empty candidate got into the payload. do you see any trailing commas or blank lines when you intercept the raw HTTP body?

 dave_customer: attached raw body from the ts-sdk (captured via tcpdump + proxy):
 ```
 {"query":"find best answer","candidates":["A","B","C",],"model":"rerank-small"}
 ```
 notice the trailing comma after C. that actually made it through to the server. python client payload did NOT have the trailing comma.

 carla_sdk: thanks, reproducer found. ts-sdk 0.9.4 has a regression in the JSON serialization path when running on Node 18 with the optional native serializer enabled — it uses a hand-rolled join for the candidates array and appends a comma unconditionally in some code paths. that yields a JSON body with a trailing comma which our NDJSON/line-splitter on the backend tolerates badly: the extra comma produces an empty candidate token which gets parsed into score 0 or NaN depending on parse path.

 carla_sdk: workaround: filter out falsy values before calling rerank, or downgrade to @redwood/inference@0.9.3. patch PR is open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/456 (fixes join & adds unit tests).

 alice_support: can you confirm whether pip redwood==0.9.3 still works for you? also if you can share request_id from the response header we can correlate logs.

 dave_customer: tried pip=0.9.3 and TS without the native serializer flag — both returned correct scores. request id: rq_02a7c9b4. i can repro locally and in staging. thanks, will stay on 0.9.3 for now.

 deploy-bot: release 0.9.5 will include the fix; target rolling deploy tomorrow 02:00 UTC.

 ben_engineer: notes for eng team:
 - root cause: ts-sdk serializer regression introduced in 0.9.4 on Node 18 when native serializer flag set.
 - impact: trailing-comma produced extra empty candidate -> backend parsing produced extra score entries (0/NaN) -> user-facing incorrect ordering.
 - severity: P2 (customer-facing, easy workaround: downgrade or filter).
 - mitigation: patch landed PR #456, releasing 0.9.5 and backend made more defensive parsing to ignore empty candidates.

 alice_support: closing the customer loop: explained workaround, confirmed downgrade works, linked PR, and scheduled release. assigning to eng-releases for postmortem and changelog blurb. :thumbsup:

 dave_customer: appreciated, thanks everyone. will re-open if anything odd after 0.9.5.
